refuted.why: A round does not run only when the token is replaced. Every deployment of stockbit-updater runs a round, including deploys without a token change. The conclusion (no schedule, so the lag recurs) still holds.
refuted.correct_statement: FACT: one round runs per deployment of stockbit-updater, including the redeploy Railway starts after a variable change. Replacing STOCKBIT_TOKEN is the documented way to start one; no schedule exists, and a push to main never starts a round. On 2026-10-27 three rounds ran between 14:18 and 14:53 UTC with an unchanged token_expires_at of 2026-10-28 10:53 UTC. After that time every round fails until a new token is set. So the broker lag recurs unless someone deploys with a valid token after each session.

additional_findings: Preset counts multiply the cost (FACT). The prototype's libCounts() evaluates every preset (25) and every saved screen over the whole universe. It runs at boot (HTML 1713), after each Bandar threshold edit (1628), and after save, delete and duplicate (1455, 1456, 1651); HTML 1187 renders the counts on the preset chips (1208). A server version needs every preset's result per as-of date. Every Bandarmology and Combined flow preset uses a fixed grid: bandar(10,3), bavg(10), broker(YP,5), fnet(20), fstreak, freq(20) xa within 3, silent(5,20,1.3,4). A fixed-grid daily snapshot, or precomputed preset counts, therefore covers all presets. This is a stronger snapshot argument than 'within N days'.

Send to Backtest handoff (FACT, HTML 1655-1670) exists in the prototype. fnet gt/lt goes to Backtest fnet; broker gt to broker; topacc to top5 (top N dropped); bandar acc/bigacc/gt to top5 > 0 (ratio and thresholds dropped). Backtest fnet, broker and top5 use all boards and the price-bar calendar (flow.ts:8-14). With a Regular-default screener, the sent conditions evaluate differently in the Backtest (168 of 841 stocks differ on 20D foreign net, 20 flip sign). Nothing breaks, because the types exist in catalog.ts:53-55, but the user should decide whether to label or translate the board.

The Terminal's shipped broker ranking uses all boards (FACT). 'Top accumulators' (DESIGN.md:38) ranks by Σ net value, All investors, All boards, default 5 sessions. A Regular-default screener can show different top brokers than the Terminal panel for the same stock. Add this to the board decision.

Monitoring gate trap (FACT). Monitoring_Stockbit_Update has a stale RUNNING row e3331473 (started 2026-10-27 14:25:02 UTC, updated_at 14:25:08, no finished_at), superseded by 51a399f1 (SUCCESS 14:28-14:53). The round before it, 3323340d, FAILED 14:18-14:24 with 'TypeError: Object of type date is not JSON serializable'. A screener gated on 'no RUNNING row' would be blocked indefinitely. Gate on the newest row by started_at being SUCCESS, or on the publisher state.json broker_through / broker_behind_sessions (ERRORS M243). Grep found neither row nor that error in ERRORS_AND_SOLUTIONS.md or RAILWAY_CHANGELOG.md, so they may be unrecorded.

Cross-table skew during a round (FACT, refresh.py). F05 is written and committed per date for all tickers at once (102-111). F02 follows per ticker (118-121), then F03 per date after all of F02 (129-130), then F06 per ticker (138-139). For most of the about 37 min, F05 already holds the new date for every ticker while F03 lacks it and F06 is partial. A snapshot that combines F05 rankings with F06 or F03 must be built only after the round reaches SUCCESS.

Pipeline risk of snapshot option (a), INFERENCE from updater.py:134-162. The broker load, features, INDEX, events and table status run in one try block. A snapshot step placed inline in refresh_broker_features or after it would, on failure, mark the round FAILED and skip INDEX, events and Database_Table_Status. It needs its own try, or must run after table_status, to keep the existing round intact. Option (b), publisher-written, does not have this coupling.

F06 physical order (FACT: pg_stats ticker corr 0.969, trade_date 0.047). Multi-date cross-sections are scattered random reads (Q2b reads about 22k blocks through 1,717 pkey searches); this explains the 3-8 s re-run times and the one timeout. The latest date is cheap (Q1: 176 heap blocks), plausibly because freshly re-inserted rows sit together (INFERENCE). Fixed-window metrics read from the latest F06 row stay in milliseconds.

Stored F06 'trade count' frequency is complete for universe stocks in 2026 (0 nulls in 161,294 Regular rows). The price table has no frequency column, so freq spike (D1) depends on broker data and therefore on the broker lag (M243), unlike volume-based metrics.
